record.notes: The order page sells this plan at USD 3.50 a year. It renews at the same rate. There is no refund at all: the order form carries a mandatory 'I understand that there are no refunds' checkbox. The operator names no company and is a single person. It is the only vendor in the sub-dollar band with a first-hand public report of WireGuard running on it: a LowEndTalk user installed precompiled wireguard-go and ran it with shadowsocks 'without running out of ram' over 255 days of uptime, and another confirms TUN/TAP can be enabled. That is a report that somebody did it, not a measurement that it works today. UDP on the 20 forwarded ports is still unstated by the vendor. | 2026-10-24: the UDP question is still open. Five pages were read - the packages page, the pricing table, the NAT IPv4 help page, the knowledge-base index and the WireGuard how-to - and none of them says whether the 20 forwarded ports carry UDP. What the vendor does say is that WireGuard should be installed with wireguard-go, which is the userspace implementation an OpenVZ guest needs when the host kernel has no module. The pricing table also puts the 256 MB rung at USD 6.50-10.00 a year (USD 0.54-0.83 a month), so a beefier Gullo box is available inside the band if UDP turns out to be fine.
